reviews.body:
Thanks a lot for this one, it's a clean fix. Grouping the fragments by `index` and keeping `id`/`type` brings the TS integration in line with the Python aggregator, and keeping the streamed text next to the tool calls is a nice touch. I ran it locally through `trackOpenAI` with a stubbed stream: two interleaved parallel calls plus leading text now come out as two separate calls with the message kept, and text-only streams are unchanged.

A few points:

1. `src/decorators.ts:242-253`, following up on the open Baz thread: yes, please add the `trackOpenAI` streaming test in this PR. No new harness is needed. A fake SDK whose `chat.completions.create` returns an async generator of chunks, plus a stub `parent` (`{ span: vi.fn(), update: vi.fn(), end: vi.fn() }`), is enough. Drain the stream and assert the whole `output` passed to `parent.span`. That covers the wiring the parser tests can't (spreading `chunkData.data`, collecting `chunkData.text`, picking the final output). Mixed text plus interleaved parallel calls, and text-only, would be the two cases to cover.
2. `tests/parsers.test.ts`: "keeps every tool call carried by a single chunk" and "orders tool calls by index when fragments arrive out of order" only compare the ids. Please assert the whole `getToolCallOutput(...)` result, as the first test does, so names, types and arguments are checked too. The same applies to "keeps the text of a chunk that also carries tool calls", which can assert the whole `parseChunk` result.
3. Minor: the ids, names and arguments could be generated (random) rather than fixed literals. That keeps the assertions from passing by coincidence.
4. Minor: formatting. This package's code is in the prettier 2 / es5 style (main's `parsers.ts` passes `npx prettier@2 --check`). With that, only two of your lines need rewrapping: the `buildStreamOutput` return type at `src/parsers.ts:538` and the `expect(buildStreamOutput(...)).toEqual({` line in the test.
5. Minor: the Testing section of the description still says 4 new tests / 22 passing. It is 6 and 26 now.

Nice work! During my testing, found the issue with gemini openai-like endpoint, which sends tool calls with no index, but it had been the issue before, so approving.
Good job!

review_comments.body:
### Streamed tool-call output wiring has no test The new stream-wrapper path is untested, so a wiring regression in tool-call accumulation or final output selection would leave the suite green; add an integration test that calls `trackOpenAI` with a mocked streaming client and asserts the recorded span output. Want Baz to fix this for you? [Activate Fixer](https://baz.co/agents/baz) You can also update your AI coding guidelines based on this comment by `apply pr to [branch name]`
Other fix methods
Prompt for AI Agents ```text Before applying, verify this suggestion against the current code. In sdks/typescript/src/opik/integrations/opik-openai/src/decorators.ts around lines 243-266, add integration coverage for the `tracedOutputGenerator` stream-wrapper logic that accumulates tool-call chunks and selects `buildStreamOutput` for the final traced output. Create a test that calls the public `trackOpenAI` with a mocked client streaming method, consumes the wrapped stream, and asserts the recorded span and parent update contain the expected output. Keep the existing parser-helper tests, but ensure this end-to-end test would fail if the stream wiring or final output selection regresses. ```

### Index order lost when tool calls stream out of order `getToolCallOutput` records tool calls in stream-arrival order, so an index 1 fragment arriving before index 0 produces `[call 1, call 0]` instead of the index order expected by the Python aggregator and tests; sort the Map keys by index before mapping. Want Baz to fix this for you? [Activate Fixer](https://baz.co/agents/baz)
Other fix methods
Prompt for AI Agents ```text Before applying, verify this suggestion against the current code. In `sdks/typescript/src/opik/integrations/opik-openai/src/parsers.ts` around line 508, update `getToolCallOutput` so the returned `tool_calls` are ordered by ascending tool-call index rather than Map insertion order. Sort the Map entries or keys numerically before mapping them to output values, preserving grouping while ensuring out-of-order streamed fragments produce the canonical call order. ```

Good catch: the calls came out in arrival order. Fixed in d76337e: tool calls are now sorted by index (as the Python aggregator does), with a test for out-of-order fragments. The same commit keeps text from a chunk that carries both content and tool calls.

The stream wrapper now only collects per-chunk results and hands the output to `buildStreamOutput`, which the new tests cover for tool calls, mixed text and text-only streams. The package has no `trackOpenAI` streaming test harness yet; happy to add one with a mocked client if you'd like it in this PR.

comments.body:
Thanks for the review. Pushed 8dbfb8f42d, which covers each point:

1. Added `tests/trackOpenAI.test.ts`: `trackOpenAI` around a fake SDK whose `chat.completions.create` returns an async generator, with a stub `parent` (`span`, `update`, `end`). It drains the stream and asserts the whole `output` passed to `parent.span`, for interleaved parallel tool calls with leading text and for a text-only stream. The parallel-calls case fails on `main`.
2. The single-chunk, out-of-order and mixed-chunk tests in `tests/parsers.test.ts` now assert the whole `getToolCallOutput(...)`, `buildStreamOutput(...)` and `parseChunk(...)` result.
3. Ids, names, arguments and text in these tests are generated per run.
4. Rewrapped the `buildStreamOutput` return type in `src/parsers.ts` the way `prettier@2` does; the new test file is `prettier@2`-clean too. The rest of the existing `parsers.test.ts` was left untouched.
5. Updated the Testing section of the description: 6 tests in `parsers.test.ts` plus 2 in `trackOpenAI.test.ts`, 28 passing.

`vitest`, `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` pass locally.
Thanks again, @pcbeingused333 — merged, and it closes #8998. Clean fix keeping streamed parallel tool calls apart in the TS OpenAI integration. 🙌
